stem.text: A particle moves along the x-axis. Its position at time t seconds is \( x(t) = - t^{3} - t^{2} + 25 t - 3 \) meters, for \( t \ge 0 \). Find the speed of the particle at time t = 2, and determine whether the speed is increasing or decreasing at that time. Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: The speed is 9 meters per second, and it is decreasing at that time, because \( v(2) = 9 \) and \( a(2) = -14 \) have opposite signs.

worked_solution.text: Velocity is the derivative of position, \( v(t) = - 3 t^{2} - 2 t + 25 \), so \( v(2) = 9 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: velocity is the derivative of position

worked_solution.text: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity, \( a(t) = - 6 t - 2 \), so \( a(2) = -14 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: acceleration is the derivative of velocity

worked_solution.text: The speed is \( \left|v(2)\right| = 9 \) meters per second.
worked_solution.rule_named: speed is the absolute value of velocity

worked_solution.text: Because \( v(2) = 9 \) and \( a(2) = -14 \) have opposite signs, the speed of the particle is decreasing at t = 2.
worked_solution.rule_named: speed increases when velocity and acceleration share a sign

options.label: The speed is 14 meters per second, and it is increasing at that time, because \( v(2) = -14 \) and \( a(2) = -6 \) have the same sign.
options.derivation: the position differentiated once too often, so the acceleration is read as the velocity and its derivative as the acceleration
